document.title: PLC MANUFACTURERS AND EVOLUTION OF CPU MODELS
document.subtitle: Documentary base for a thesis on hardware obsolescence in industrial automation
document.rigor_criterion: CRITERION OF RIGOR. This document lists real CPU and controller models in technological order, from older generations to recent ones. No years, part numbers or EOL statuses are invented. Where an official public source does not show the exact part number of a generation, the document says so expressly instead of filling the data in by approximation. For the IPC manufacturers (Advantech, Kontron and AAEON), industrial computer models and their processor platform are listed, because they are not PLCs with an equivalent modular CPU.
how_to_read: The order of the rows within each manufacturer runs from older generations towards more recent ones, according to the technical documentation consulted.
'Family' is not the same as 'CPU model'. That is why, whenever the source allows it, the exact code is shown (for example, Siemens CPU 315-2 DP or Rockwell 1756-L75).

This version gives priority to accuracy. It does not claim that each list is the absolute inventory of every SKU manufactured in the whole history of each company; it represents the sequence of models that it was possible to verify from documentation without inventing data.
Release, EOL and successor dates will be added in a later layer of the matrix, and only where dated, verifiable evidence exists for each model.

verification_remarks.decision: The official Emerson source confirms the migration from the Series 90-30 to PACSystems. In this version no IC693CPU numbers from the Series 90-30 were transcribed, because the official search consulted did not present a reliable table with those codes. Verified RX3i codes are included.

The official Hitachi release confirms four functional HX models (standard, high-function, motion and redundancy), but it does not show the part numbers in the public table. That is why no codes were invented.

FATEK maintains an official M PLC CPU Unit manual updated in 2026. The public result consulted did not show the individual CPU codes; the designation M Series / CPU Unit is kept until a catalog with explicit part numbers is obtained.
The PFC300 family is documented, but in this version the 750-830X pattern is kept wherever the exact full part number was not checked model by model.
Advantech, Kontron and AAEON are kept for the analysis of industrial computing obsolescence. Their models must not be treated statistically as PLC CPUs without first separating the hardware category.
